newsitem.title: GERMANY: Berlin remembers murdered Jews on Holocaust day.
newsitem.headline: Berlin remembers murdered Jews on Holocaust day.

text.p: Berliners marked world Holocaust memorial day on Sunday by reading aloud the names of the nearly 56,000 Berlin Jews murdered under the Nazis -- a list that is so long it takes 26 hours to read out.
The youth group of international Jewish organisation B'nai B'rith erected a small tent in front of the busy Wittenbergplatz underground station for the reading.

Group members and their families, local politicians and Holocaust survivors, read the 55,696 names from a volume the size of a telephone book, as passers-by stopped to listen and light memorial candles. Some who had come to hear the names of family members read out wept quietly.

B'nai B'rith members began reading late on Saturday evening under the motto "Every person has a name", starting with Jutta Aal, a woman born in Bavaria in 1860 and killed at Theresienstadt death camp on September 1, 1942.

Ester Wolff, a 62-year-old Holocaust survivor, said she had chosen to read a page of names for personal reasons, although she did not want to look through the record book to find the names of her relatives and friends.

"I know they are dead and you can't bring the dead back," Wolff said. "But I wanted to draw attention to the people one more time. Even if no one listened today, I know it helps me a little bit to be here."
Organisers estimated they would finish at midnight on Sunday, with the name of Leo Zyzman, a native Berliner who was murdered at Auschwitz on July 24, 1942 at the age of 16.
In the 1920s, more than 170,000 Jews lived in Berlin, representing a third of all German Jews at the time.
Memorial ceremonies for the holiday, called Jom HaShoa in Hebrew, were scheduled worldwide.
